summary: Cross-border-reporting accountability specificity and cube-axis correction pass.
major_judgments: The riskiest unfinished surface after rev0299 was cross-border reporting, because generic profiles there can hide treaty-relief paywalls, withholding overcollection, remittance corridor rents, status-access ransom, source-state erasure, and claim-split implementation failure.

Cross-border responsibility must follow control over coordination tables, customs/CBAM registries, remittance rails, KYC gates, fee-waiver/status portals, withholding/reclaim/MAP channels, GIR exchange, apportionment formulas, and fallback dispute or capacity duties—not foreignness, visible remitter status, claimant status, or legal-remitter labels.

The international coordination claim-split and UN-inclusive coordination records had the most important cube-template defects: they looked like generic foreign-record routes rather than GIR/exchange, capacity, fiscal-agency, source-state, host-burden, and claim-split routes; rev0300 corrects those axis profiles.
Continue clearing bounded families before building archetypes; remaining placeholder clusters are now small enough to clear together in the next targeted pass.
